data.name: Petronella
data.gender_notes: Petronella is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Roman family name Petronius, derived from the Latin word 'petra', meaning 'rock'. In Christian tradition, Petronella is the name of a Spanish saint and martyr who was beheaded during the Moorish invasion in the 8th century. The name Petronella carries the meaning “Rock, Stone” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Petronella usually hope their child will grow to embody rock, stone and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A strong and enduring name, symbolizing faith and steadfastness in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Petronella belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rock, Stone.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Petronella total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Petronella is a beautiful and rich name rooted in the history and culture of the Spanish people. It carries the legacy of the Roman family name Petronius, which is renowned for its strength and resilience, much like the petra or rock from which it is derived. This name also celebrates the ancient Heritage of the Spanish people, who have preserved and passed down the stories of their saints and martyrs like Petronella, inspiring generations with their courage and faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Petronella holds deep spiritual significance, representing the unwavering faith and courage of a Christian martyr. In the Christian tradition, the name evokes images of Petronella, the Spanish saint, who was beheaded during the Moorish invasion in the 8th century. Her name, which means 'rock' in Latin, symbolizes the unshakable faith she had in God. Petronella's story continues to inspire and encourage believers, reminding us of the power of faith and the importance of remaining steadfast in our beliefs, even in the face of adversity.
